paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. God says to Solomon, "Ask, and I will give it to you!" (1 Kings 3:5). That is a blank check, and Solomon doesn't grab for gold or a long life. He says he is "only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in," and asks for "an understanding heart" (1 Kings 3:7, 9).

So what's the lesson? Solomon starts by admitting what he doesn't know, and then he asks God for exactly what the job needs. I think that's the whole secret, baker. I have stamped cookies crooked for years before I would admit I needed help, and Solomon figured it out on day one. It pleased the Lord that he asked for this (1 Kings 3:10).

And look what God does with that kind of asking. He gives the wise and discerning heart, and then He gives "both riches and honor," which Solomon never requested (1 Kings 3:12, 13). Then comes the "if": "if you walk in My ways and keep My statutes and commandments, just as your father David did, I will prolong your days" (1 Kings 3:14). So when you don't know the way, baker, ask God for understanding first, and keep walking in His ways after you get it.
